newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products firm, dollar hits gas oil trading.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products firm, dollar hits gas oil trading.

text.p: NWE oil products all firmed on Monday as futures pushed higher, while the steadily rising dollar deadened gas oil trading, dealers said.

Gasoline traded once at $186 fob AR, a gain of some $2/$3 a tonne from Friday, but the market was mostly quiet with bids and offers some distance apart. Late morning Rotterdam offers were at around $187/$188 fob. Bids were some $3/$4 below.
Heating oil barges were similarly $2/$3 higher as IPE August gas oil futures pushed higher.
Rotterdam offers were unchanged at IPE August +$1.
Bids were notionally at August screen flat, but buyers appeared non-existent as the dollar's rise against the mark continued, killing demand in the key German market.
The dollar pushed past DM1.79, its highest level since August 1991.
"The deutschmark is in free-fall. It's killing activity. There are no bidders at this level," one German trader said.
High sulphur fuel oil gained about $1 with trades in the range $86.25-$87.25 fob Rotterdam for stored product. Running refinery offers were at $87.50 by late morning.
